summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR5,240 crores and EBITDA 33% to INR756 crores; FY26 PAT INR1,061 crores (+17%) and a new INR2,700 crore capex was approved.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as one of the strongest quarters on record, with revenue of INR5,240 crores (+27% YoY, +19% QoQ), total EBITDA of INR756 crores (+33% YoY) and PAT of INR312 crores (+42% YoY). Volumes grew 22% YoY in Q4 and FY26 volumes were 4.94 million tonnes (+26%). The Board approved a fresh INR2,700 crore capex across a Kharagpur long/specialty wire mill and a Sambalpur stainless steel expansion with downstream lines, both targeted for March 2029, mainly funded by internal accruals. Management guided to FY27 EBITDA growth of around 30%, while stating a conservative stance.

financial_highlights.value: INR2.7 per share (27% of INR10 face value)

segments.name: Carbon steel / steel products
segments.commentary: Steel products contributed about 75% of revenue in both Q4 and FY26; carbon steel was about 39% of revenue, the largest single contributor. CR coil volume in Q4 was 50,344 tonnes (about +200% YoY) on ramp-up of the Jamuria CRM complex.

segments.name: Stainless steel
segments.commentary: Q4 volume was 27,287 tonnes (+13% YoY) and realisation rose about 17% YoY. Management said the Odisha (Sambalpur) plant will carry about 80% integration with existing operations.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Realisation rose 16% YoY to INR4,07,461 per tonne. A new caster, foil stock and foil plant are being commissioned this year, with battery foil qualified with 2 to 3 customers.

segments.name: Pig iron and iron pellets
segments.commentary: Pig iron volume was 2,03,499 tonnes in Q4 (about +200% YoY). Iron pellet volume was 2,78,341 tonnes (+40% YoY).

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA growth of around 30% over FY26, per Chairman; CFO said FY27 will at least match FY26 as full-year impact of new capacities comes through.
CRM complex EBITDA expected at about INR10,000-11,000 per tonne in FY27; aluminium EBITDA expected at INR35,000-40,000 per tonne.
Galvalume line at Jamuria to be commissioned around end-May or early June 2026; colour-coated volume expected to roughly double YoY.
0.5 million tonne DRI/sponge iron facility to be commissioned in FY27; aluminium plant commissioning in H1 FY27, with the impact expected in H2.

Capex: total program about INR10,000 crores, with about INR2,900 crores in FY27 and about INR3,000 crores in FY28, balance in the following two years. Separate 800,000-tonne steel plant with SMS shop targeted by end of next year.
Debt policy caps total debt at 0.5x total equity; cash generation of INR2,000-2,500 crores expected over time to fund the capex.
capex_capacity: INR2,700 crore new capex approved: long specialty wire mill with furnace at Kharagpur, 8 lakh tonnes capacity, INR900 crores, target 31 March 2029.

Sambalpur (Odisha) stainless steel expansion to 6 million tonnes with cold rolling, precision cold rolling, hot rolling handling and pickling line and bright annealing line; INR1,800 crores, target March 2029; mainly internal accruals.
CRM complex Phase 2 at Jamuria commissioned in Q4/April 2026; blast furnace at Kharagpur commissioned in FY26; aluminium downstream heat treatment commissioned at Pakuria in Q4.
Planned 800,000-tonne steel plant with SMS shop; separate HR flat product plant at roughly one-third of the cost of a standard 2 million tonne HR plant, per management.
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 realisations improved across most product lines; CR coil/CR sheet realisation rose about 15% YoY to INR78,513 per tonne.
Management said aluminium exports are oversold and the company cannot supply the international market; aluminium pricing is largely a pass-through.
Nickel-linked costs are passed through to stainless customers with some inventory lag; about 70-75% of the stainless portfolio is low or no-nickel grades.
Management guided that Q4 realisations are unlikely to rise further from current levels, citing the monsoon session and market conditions.
On the Q4 steel EBITDA per tonne question, management attributed part of the gap to old low-priced carryover orders and part to import cost and rupee impact; no quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FY26 volume growth, and which capacities come online in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 0.5 million tonnes of DRI, the Galvalume line at Jamuria, doubling colour-coated volume, new captive power plants lowering grid power costs, and the aluminium foil plant.

qa_highlights.question: Is aluminium a pass-through business or does it earn higher margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely a pass-through in price terms; margin upside expected from backward integration into foil stock as the new foil plant is built.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 EBITDA exceed INR3,000 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the estimate was close, plus or minus about 5%, and pointed to about 30% growth in FY27 as achievable, with conservative guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise and payable days stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said inventory rose from 99 to 123 days due to positioning of raw materials for CRM, blast furnace coking coal and iron ore, to be liquidated in Q1-Q2 FY27. Payable days are about 130 and not a one-off.

qa_highlights.question: What are the returns and EBITDA per tonne expectations for the stainless steel capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects EBITDA of INR15,000-20,000 per tonne for stainless, about INR12,000-15,000 on an overall basis, and above INR18,000 for an integrated iron-to-steel route. Returns are said to be 20-30% better than carbon steel.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded and what is the balance-sheet stance?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly internal accruals with possible short-term debt. Management said net cash was about INR1,800-1,900 crores in FY26 and expected to exceed INR2,000 crores. Debt capped at 0.5x equity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ED matter and the CPCB non-compliance a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ED coal case is at the letter-reply stage and not a concern. On CPCB, it described a minor error found in inspection that it has rectified, with compliance expected within 3 months.

risks_watch: Inventory days rose to 123 from 99 and payable days are about 130; management expects liquidation in Q1-Q2 FY27, so working-capital reversal is a watch item.
Q4 steel EBITDA per tonne rose only about INR2,600 against a price increase of about INR5,100; cost drivers were not quantified.
Nickel price increases (about 20% since December per an analyst) and imported raw material costs affecting stainless margins.
Pending ED notice on coal and a CPCB non-compliance observation; management says both are manageable.
Execution of the INR2,700 crore capex by March 2029 and the aluminium foil ramp-up in H2 FY27.
Management has stated that Q4 realisations are unlikely to move higher from current levels.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, margins and cash generation, with a stated conservative stance on guidance. Evasive on the Q4 cost-versus-price bridge and on the ED matter, where questions were deflected to a separate discussion.
key_quotes: This is a business firing on all cylinders.
Shyam Metalics will never depend on the realization side.
I think this year, we will be very comfortable with our growth close to 30% over this year.
